I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against Du for their mishandling of my service upgrade and subsequent billing issues. Despite multiple attempts to resolve this matter directly with Du, I have faced persistent issues that remain unresolved, compelling me to seek your assistance.
On 31st May, a team from Du visited my premises to upgrade my service from 4G to 5G. During this visit, I explicitly instructed the team to cancel the 4G service upon completion of the 5G installation. The team assured me that this would be done. However, this did not happen, resulting in a bill that included charges for both 4G and 5G services last month, causing me to pay double.
I filed a complaint regarding the cancellation of the 4G service and requested an adjustment in the bill to reflect this mistake. Although the 4G service was eventually cancelled, no adjustment was made to my bill. I contacted customer care on 6th July, and the executive assured me that I could proceed with the payment for the 5G service and that a refund for the excess 4G charges would be arranged. Following this, I made the payment for the 5G services on the same day.
However, a few days later, my internet was abruptly disconnected, I was unable to access the Du application. Upon contacting customer care again, I was informed that my internet had been suspended due to an outstanding payment. Despite explaining the situation and the previous assurances I received, I was told that no such commitment was found in their records, which I find incorrect. I had no choice but to pay the surplus amount to restore my internet service.
A week later, I received the bill for the next billing cycle, which was again incorrect, as it was twice the amount for 5G services. When I contacted customer care, they informed that 4G connection was cancelled after the billing cycle date, hence the additional charges. After explaining the complete history again, executive assured me on 19th July 2024 that he had escalated the issue to their billing team for a reversal of surplus charges, and it would be credited on priority basis.
Today, 21st July 2024, I followed up again, only to be informed that all the charges are deemed valid and no reversal will be made. Du's reasoning is that the communication regarding the cancellation of the 4G service at the time of the 5G installation was verbal, and they claim no proof is available. However, I must emphasize that these communications were with Du-authorized personnel, and as a customer, I believe they would be credible. It is unreasonable to expect customers to record verbal communications when Du representatives are in their homes performing installations.
As a result of these issues, I have incurred excess charges amounting to 416 AED. This response is unacceptable, considering the numerous assurances I received and the clear mishandling of my service upgrade and billing.
I respectfully request your intervention to resolve this matter.

Dear TDRA,
I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the M2M service we have taken from Etisalat for our SIM cards. Despite the regulatory mandate from TDRA requiring Etisalat to notify customers of over-usage, we did not receive any such notifications during our testing phase. Given this context, we are requesting a waiver of the excessive charges for the March bill and an adjustment to reflect the standard data plan charges.

SPFeedback:
TDRA has reviewed your complaint and has exchanged related correspondence with your service provider (Etisalat) on your behalf.
We wish to bring your attention to the results of the investigation as follows:

1: The complaint was raised to the concerned team for further investigation.
2: According to the system, the M2M service was activated on August 10, 2023, to be used for tracking systems.
3: After reviewing the service provider proposal, and the signed contract, we found that you did not select the data hard cap option to be activated in the contract.
4: This service depended on data as the main use for tracking, and the default for this service is CAP open since the device wouldn`t lost if data is consumed.
5: As discussed with you during the call, you can check and manage your Data usage via the portal provided by the service provider, as all the usage will show in the same portal live.
6: Moreover, the service provider can't set the data hard cap unless it was selected or requested by the customer to avoid device loss, and this will be your responsibility.
7: Therefore, all the charges shall remain valid.
